Glassy alloy ribbons with a cross section of 0.02 /C2 1.2 mm 2 were also produced by the melt spinning method.
Only broad peaks without crystalline peak can be seen for all these bulk samples, indicating the formation of a glassy phase in the diameter range up to 5 mm.

It is noticed that this Fe-based bulk glassy alloy rod exhibits very high strength of 4170 MPa combined with plastic strain of about 0.0025.
In addition, Vickers hardness number was measured as 1225.
A localized main shear band can be observed on the surface of the rod as shown in Fig. 7, and its angle with stress axis is measured to be 44 /C176, which is in agreement with the other results [18].
These high values are interpreted to result from strong bonding nature among the constituent elements as is expected from the mixing enthalpies with large negative values.
The agreement also indicates that the Fe-based bulk glassy alloys have an elastic–plastic deformation mode without appreciable work hardening.
